Recipe Reel (Product as Ingredient).definition: A food-creator style recipe video: opens on the finished, craveable dish/drink (or a 'best drink I ever made' hook), then shows the recipe built step by step with the product added as one ingredient (pack shot mid-way), and closes on the money shot / first bite.
Recipe Reel (Product as Ingredient).why: It looks like native recipe content people save and share, so the product gets screen time inside something useful instead of a pitch; ideal for consumables (powders, oils, drink mixes, sauces, supplements).
how: Pick a craveable, trending recipe (mocktail, s'mores bars, protein bites) where your product is a natural ingredient.
Open on the finished result, then shoot hands/creator assembling it step by step with a clear branded pack shot as the product goes in.
End on the bite/sip reaction or hero shot with recipe card text and a soft CTA.
Recipe Reel (Product as Ingredient).closest_existing: UGC How-To / Product Demo - those show how to use the product itself; here the ad is a recipe and the product is just one ingredient in a bigger dish.

Animated Character Story (Pixar / Cartoo.definition: The whole ad is a short animated story (Pixar-style 3D or hand-drawn 2D picture book) with a human or pet protagonist: opens on the character living the problem, middle shows failed fixes then discovering the product, close shows the happy 'after' and a product end card.
Animated Character Story (Pixar / Cartoo.why: Cartoon storytelling stops the scroll, lets you dramatize embarrassing or invisible problems (bloating, acne, a sick dog) without real actors, and is cheap to make with AI video.
how: Write a 30-60s first- or third-person story: problem moment, what they tried that failed, discovery of the product, life after.
Generate a consistent Pixar-style or storybook character and animate each beat as a scene, with captions/voiceover.
Show the real product clearly at the discovery beat and end on a product card with offer.
Animated Character Story (Pixar / Cartoo.closest_existing: Claymation / Talking Objects - Claymation is a different style and Talking Objects has the product or body part narrating; here an animated person/pet acts out a problem-to-solution story.

Set Up With Me (Space Makeover).definition: A 'come set up / reset with me' video: opens on a bare, messy or outdated space (stripped bed, empty wall, cluttered counter), the creator unpacks and installs or styles the product in quick satisfying steps, and it closes on a slow pan of the finished 'dream' space.
Set Up With Me (Space Makeover).why: The before-to-after build is satisfying to watch and lets the viewer picture the product in their own home; best for home decor, bedding, furniture, organizers and wall art.
how: Start on the space looking plain or tired (or the sealed package next to it) with a POV caption like 'the bed of my dreams'.
Film fast hands-on steps of putting the product in: fitting sheets, hanging the piece, placing items, with close-ups of texture and the logo tag.
End on a styled wide shot of the finished space with soft lighting or a cosy moment (candle, pet, lying down).
Set Up With Me (Space Makeover).closest_existing: Unboxing / Product Demo - Unboxing stops at the first open and Demo shows the product working; here the whole ad is installing the product into a room and revealing the transformed space.

Aesthetic Room Tour (Styled Space Walkth.definition: A silent, music-led handheld/gimbal walkthrough of one beautifully styled room or home: opens on a 'pov: the life I want' / 'small bedrooms can still be beautiful' caption over a wide shot, glides past details (bed, lamp, shelves, textures), and closes on the full room with a 'shop the look' line.
Aesthetic Room Tour (Styled Space Walkth.why: It sells the aspirational lifestyle, not the item; the viewer wants the whole room and the products come with it. Works for home decor, furniture and bedding brands with an influencer-styled space.
how: Style one room fully with your products (or partner with a home influencer whose room already looks great).
Shoot slow gimbal glides and detail close-ups in warm golden light, with a short aspirational POV caption on top.
Cut to trending calm music, end on the hero wide shot with 'shop the collection' or a price/offer line.
Aesthetic Room Tour (Styled Space Walkth.closest_existing: Day In The Life / Satisfying B-roll - no person's routine or random b-roll here; the whole ad is a guided tour of a styled room as the aspiration.

Before/After Transformation Reveal (Glow.definition: The whole ad is one transformation: opens on the 'before' (shaggy hair in the barber chair, frizzy curls, a 'Day 0' body/face), the middle shows the product doing the work (a pro cutting and styling with it, or an AI morph sliding from Day 0 to Day 90), and it closes on the big 'after' reveal plus product card/offer.
Before/After Transformation Reveal (Glow.why: A visible change from bad to great is the strongest proof there is and the viewer watches to see the reveal; use for hair, skin, body, cleaning or any product with a visual result. Live-action (salon/barber chair) builds trust, the AI-morph version is a cheap 10s test.
how: Pick the most dramatic 'before' you can show (real client in the chair, or an AI-generated Day 0 image) with a hook caption like 'every transformation…' or 'Face fat? gone'.
Show the product in action mid-ad: pro applying/styling it, or a smooth morph with the product pack sitting in frame.
Hold on the 'after' (turn, hair flip, Day 90 label), then cut to a clean product shot with price/offer.
Before/After Transformation Reveal (Glow.closest_existing: Challenge / Case Studies - those follow a person over days or break down a result in talk; here the ad is just the before → product → after reveal, either a live makeover or an AI morph.

AI Before/After Morph.definition: 6-15s ad: an AI-generated body part or face morphs from 'Day 0' to 'Day 90' with the product pack in frame, then cuts to a product card with price and code.
AI Before/After Morph.why: Variant of the transformation reveal; cheap and fast to test, but all IN examples are one brand.
how: Generate a Day 0 and Day 90 image of the problem area.
Morph between them with the product pack overlaid and a punchy headline.
End on a product card with price per day and a code.

Input vs Result (Custom-Made Reveal).definition: Rapid paired montage for a custom/made-to-order product: opens on a caption like 'the stones our clients chose vs the rings we made', then alternates 'the stone' / 'the inspiration' shots with the finished piece made from it, and closes on 'design yours' with the brand logo.
Input vs Result (Custom-Made Reveal).why: Each pair is a mini reveal that proves craftsmanship and makes the viewer imagine their own version; ideal for personalised/custom products (custom jewellery, pet portraits, photo gifts, engraved items).
how: Collect 4-8 pairs of customer input (photo, stone, sketch, inspiration image) and the finished product made from it.
Cut them as quick labelled pairs ('the photo' / 'the portrait') over trending music, close-up and hand-held.
End on a line like 'Send us yours / design your own' with the logo and offer.
Input vs Result (Custom-Made Reveal).closest_existing: Product Comparison Video - that compares against a competitor or old method; here each pair is the customer's raw input next to the custom piece made from it.

Stop-Motion Product Showcase.definition: A 6-10s frame-by-frame stop-motion of the real product and props (no clay, no people): opens on the product alone or a closed case, items pop in, stack, pack or swap frame by frame to build a flat lay or scene, and it closes on the finished arrangement with one line of copy.
Stop-Motion Product Showcase.why: The jerky 'magic' motion stops the scroll and shows many features or bundle items in seconds with no talent; great cheap test for accessories, bundles, luggage, beauty kits and gifts.
how: Shoot top-down or locked-off on a clean backdrop; move the product and props a little between each photo.
Build a story in 40-80 frames: empty to full flat lay, unpacked to packed case, or one colourway swapping to the next.
Add one short headline ('Overpack. It fits.') and end on the finished arrangement with logo.
Stop-Motion Product Showcase.closest_existing: Claymation - same frame-by-frame technique, but here it is the real product and props building a scene, not clay characters telling a story.

Prop Analogy Explainer (Physical Mechani.definition: An expert in a white coat (or just hands) explains how the problem works using an everyday object as a stand-in for the body: opens on the prop and a hook ('nobody wants to be the short kid', 'double cleansing: scam?'), the middle acts the mechanism out on the prop (orange peel = pores, tube = urethra, pool noodle = growth plate, straw = blood vessel), and it closes with the product as the fix plus offer.
Prop Analogy Explainer (Physical Mechani.why: A physical analogy makes an invisible mechanism instantly understandable and believable, and the odd prop is a pattern-interrupt hook; best for supplements, skincare and health devices.
how: Pick one cheap prop that mirrors the body part or problem (fruit for skin, hose for veins, sponge for gut lining).
Script 30-60s where every claim is shown on the prop: the problem happening, why common fixes fail, what your product's ingredient does.
Bring the product into frame next to the prop for the fix, then end with the offer.
Prop Analogy Explainer (Physical Mechani.closest_existing: Fake Doctor / Animated Mechanism Explainer - Fake Doctor is a spoken endorsement and the Mechanism Explainer is animation; here the mechanism is acted out on a physical everyday prop, with or without a presenter.
